subject: science
passage: In many households in India and Pakistan, dried neem leaves have long been tucked among stored grain or folded clothes to keep insects away. Chemists studying the neem tree have isolated a compound, azadirachtin, that helps explain the practice: concentrated mainly in the seeds, it discourages many insects from feeding and disrupts the hormones that control their molting. <u>Unlike many synthetic insecticides, azadirachtin breaks down within days when exposed to sunlight.</u> That instability limits how long a single application protects a crop, but it also means the compound is unlikely to linger in soil and water, a trade-off that has made neem extracts attractive to farmers who wish to reduce lasting chemical residues.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It explains why dried neem leaves work well when placed among stored grain.
choices.B: It suggests that synthetic insecticides are more effective than azadirachtin.
choices.C: It introduces a property that the text then treats as both a drawback and a benefit.
choices.D: It offers further support for the explanation of the household practice described earlier.

explanation.why: The underlined sentence states that azadirachtin breaks down quickly in sunlight. The next sentence calls this "instability" a limit on how long it protects a crop "but" also a reason it will not "linger in soil and water." So the sentence sets up a property presented as a trade-off.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The household practice was explained in the previous sentence; breaking down in sunlight has nothing to do with leaves stored indoors.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The sentence compares how long the compounds last, not how well they work, and the text never ranks their effectiveness.
explanation.C: Correct. The quick breakdown shortens protection but also limits residues, which is the "trade-off" named in the last sentence.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The sentence shifts from the household practice to crop use; it adds nothing to the explanation of why leaves repel insects.
